rows.jp: 彼女はいつも一人だった。
rows.en: She was always alone.

ghs.en: That girl was always alone.

rows.jp: 親族や使用人の誰とも、交わろうとはしなかった。
rows.en: She made no attempt to associate with any of her relatives or the servants.

ghs.en:
She had no desire to mingle with anybody, neither
the relatives nor the employees.

rows.jp: 孤高の君―――
rows.en: My proud, solitary lady—

ghs.en: You who stand above---
ghs.assessment: 孤高の君 is the private epithet Taichi gives the aloof, solitary girl. 'You who stand above' turns it into direct address and fails to function as a title.

highlights.text: You who stand above---

rows.jp: 俺は、彼女を内心でそう呼んでいた。
rows.en: That was what I called her in my head.

ghs.en:
That is what I called her in my innermost
thoughts.

rows.jp: 言葉をかわしたことはない。
rows.en: We had never exchanged a word.

ghs.en: There had never been exchange of words.
ghs.assessment: The two had never exchanged words. 'There had never been exchange of words' omits an article and both participants.

highlights.text: There had never been exchange of words.

rows.jp: 気にはなっていた。
rows.en: But I was curious about her.

ghs.en: My interest had been piqued.

rows.jp: 屋敷がどのような人々によって維持され、いかなる経緯をたどってこの有様になったのか、俺は知らない。
rows.en: I don't know what kind of people kept the estate running, or what chain of events brought it to its present state.

ghs.en:
I don't know what kind of people maintain the
mansion or how, or even the particulars of how
things were made to be the way they were.

rows.jp: ただそこは、時の流れから隔絶された楽園のごとき場所だった。
rows.en: It was simply a place like paradise, sealed away from the flow of time.

ghs.en:
Just that this place was like Eden, separated
from the flow of time.

rows.jp: 住むのもまた、浮世離れした人々で。
rows.en: And its residents were equally removed from the ordinary world.

ghs.en:
The residents were, themselves, the people of
a secluded faraway world.

rows.jp: ときおり俺は彼女らに招かれ、甘い飲み物を振る舞われた。
rows.en: From time to time, the ladies invited me in and served me sweet drinks.

ghs.en:
On occasion I was invited by the girls, and
treated to something sweet to drink.
ghs.assessment: 彼女ら refers to the women or ladies of the household in this context. 'Girls' changes their age and register.

highlights.text:
On occasion I was invited by the girls, and
treated to something sweet to drink.

rows.jp: 着飾り、茶を楽しみ、人を招き、散策。
rows.en: Dressing up. Taking tea. Receiving guests. Strolling the grounds.

ghs.en:
Dressing up, enjoying tea, welcoming people in,
strolling.

rows.jp: 毎月頭には大量の書物・衣類・嗜好品が届いた。
rows.en: At the beginning of every month, enormous shipments of books, clothes, and luxuries arrived.

ghs.en:
At the beginning of each month, a huge quantity
of books, clothes, luxury food and consumables
were delivered.
ghs.assessment: 嗜好品 means luxury or indulgence goods. 'Luxury food and consumables' splits it into unsupported categories.

highlights.text:
At the beginning of each month, a huge quantity
of books, clothes, luxury food and consumables
were delivered.

rows.jp: 広い庭。
rows.en: A vast garden.

ghs.en: A huge garden...

rows.jp: 庭師という人々もいた。
rows.en: There were people called gardeners, too.

ghs.en: There were also people called gardeners.

rows.jp: 人里離れ、地代が安いことを差し引いても、なお広漠(こうばく)たるものがあった。
rows.en: Even allowing for its remote location and cheap land, the grounds were astonishingly vast.

ghs.en:
Even taking into account that land rent was cheap
and that it was distant from human populated
areas, it was still almost boundlessly huge.

rows.jp: 小さな俺にとって、お屋敷は広大無辺(こうだいむへん)な世界そのものだったのだ。
rows.en: To my small self, the estate was a whole world, boundless in every direction.

ghs.en:
For me, small back then, the residence was the
whole infinitely wide world itself.

rows.jp: 実際、屋敷時代以前の記憶はない。
rows.en: In fact, I have no memories from before my life there.

ghs.en:
In truth, I have no memories of a time before
the mansion.

rows.jp: 世界と屋敷は同じ大きさだった。
rows.en: The world and the estate were the same size.

ghs.en: The world and the mansion had the same huge size.

rows.jp: ある頃からか、俺はご婦人がたに気に入られるようになった。
rows.en: At some point, the ladies took a liking to me.

ghs.en:
Ever since somewhen, I had been of interest to the
older ladies.
ghs.assessment: ある頃からか means 'from some point on.' 'Ever since somewhen' uses a nonstandard word and malformed time expression.

highlights.text:
Ever since somewhen, I had been of interest to the
older ladies.

rows.jp: 女のような顔をしている、とのこと。
rows.en: Because, they said, I had a girl's face.

ghs.en: For having a face like a woman's, that is.

rows.jp: また俺の白い髪と、間近で見るとわかる不思議な模様を描く瞳も、彼女たちを退屈させなかった。
rows.en: My white hair and the strange patterns in my eyes, visible only up close, kept them entertained as well.

ghs.en:
As I also had white hair, and an inexplicable
design drawn on my pupils that could be seen
when looked at closely, I never bored them.
ghs.assessment: The unusual pattern is in Taichi's eyes or irises, not specifically drawn on his pupils. The English repeats the narrower anatomical error.

highlights.text:
As I also had white hair, and an inexplicable
design drawn on my pupils that could be seen
when looked at closely, I never bored them.

rows.jp: 少女の着るような（それもとりわけ華美な）ドレスを着させられた。
rows.en: They dressed me in the sort of dresses little girls wore—and especially gaudy ones at that.

ghs.en:
I was made to wear a girl's (and, above all,
pompously gaudy) dress.

rows.jp: そしてお茶の相手。
rows.en: Then I served as their companion for tea.

ghs.en: And then, I was a tea companion.

rows.jp: 子供にお茶の味などわからない。
rows.en: A child knows nothing about the taste of tea.

ghs.en: Children don't understand the flavor of tea.

rows.jp: でもつきあった。
rows.en: But I played along.

ghs.en: But I kept company.
ghs.assessment: Taichi nevertheless kept the ladies company. 'I kept company' normally requires the person accompanied.

highlights.text: But I kept company.

rows.jp: 砂糖菓子めいて甘やかな人々に対し、逆らうという選択肢はなかった。
rows.en: Defiance was not an option with people as sweet as spun sugar.

ghs.en:
Against those people as sweet as confectionery
a choice labeled opposition did not exist.
ghs.assessment: He had no option to resist the cloyingly sweet people. 'Against those people ... a choice labeled opposition did not exist' is a rigid and ungrammatical calque.

highlights.text:
Against those people as sweet as confectionery
a choice labeled opposition did not exist.

rows.jp: ……イヤではなかったし。
rows.en: ...Not that I disliked it.

ghs.en: ...and it wasn't something I disliked.

rows.jp: こうして幼い子供らに馬乗りにされ髪引かれる玩具業務から離れた俺は、新しい仕事として人形業務に就くことになった。
rows.en: And so, freed from toy duty—little children riding me and pulling my hair—I was assigned a new job: doll duty.

ghs.en:
And thus I was taken from the job of letting
little children ride horseback as they pulled
my hair, and I began a new job in the role of
a doll.
ghs.assessment: Small children rode astride him and pulled his hair as part of his toy role. 'The job of letting' them do it implies voluntary permission.

highlights.text:
And thus I was taken from the job of letting
little children ride horseback as they pulled
my hair, and I began a new job in the role of
a doll.

rows.jp: そんな俺を、彼女……孤高の君はひややかな視線で見ていた。
rows.en: The girl herself—my proud, solitary lady—watched me with a cold gaze.

ghs.en:
And I was like that when she... you who stand
above looked at me with cold-heartedness in her
sight.
ghs.assessment: The solitary girl regarded Taichi with a cold gaze. The English begins 'I was like that when,' shifts the epithet into direct address, and never forms a coherent subject-predicate relation.

highlights.text:
And I was like that when she... you who stand
above looked at me with cold-heartedness in her
sight.

rows.jp: いや、見てさえいなかった。
rows.en: No. She did not even look at me.

ghs.en: No, she wasn't even looking.

rows.jp: 興味がないらしく、視線はいつも俺を素通りしていった。
rows.en: Apparently uninterested, she always looked straight through me.

ghs.en:
Her sight always passed through me as if I simply
did not exist, as if there was no interest in me.

rows.jp: 支倉曜子。
rows.en: Yoko Hasekura.

ghs.en: Hasekura Youko,

rows.jp: 末娘。
rows.en: The youngest daughter.

ghs.en: youngest of the girls there.
ghs.assessment: 末娘 identifies Youko as the youngest daughter. 'Youngest of the girls there' omits the family relation.

highlights.text: youngest of the girls there.

rows.jp: ただ家族からは、それほど可愛がられている様子はない。
rows.en: Yet her family did not seem to dote on her much.

ghs.en: There wasn't that much affection from her family.

rows.jp: むしろ疎んじられていた。
rows.en: If anything, they shunned her.

ghs.en: More like, she was being shunned.

rows.jp: なるほど確かに彼女は、なかば夢幻の住人であるご婦人がたとは、違う世界に生きていた。
rows.en: It was true: she lived in a different world from the ladies, who themselves seemed half to inhabit a dream.

ghs.en:
I see, it's certain, she lives in a different
world from that of the ladies that half-dwell
in fantasy.

rows.jp: ……現実という世界に。
rows.en: ...The world called reality.

ghs.en: ...in the world called reality.

rows.jp: 一度、掃除の人夫として駆り出されたことがある。
rows.en: Once, I was pressed into service as a laborer on a cleaning job.

ghs.en:
Once, it happened that I was tossed out when I
was working as a cleaning man.
ghs.assessment: Taichi was once pressed into service as cleaning labor. 'Was tossed out when I was working as a cleaning man' instead says that he was ejected or dismissed.

highlights.text:
Once, it happened that I was tossed out when I
was working as a cleaning man.

rows.jp: 人形ハジメマシタ、以前のことだ。
rows.en: This was before I started doll duty.

ghs.en: It was before the Time of the Doll had begun,

rows.jp: 使用人さんたちにまじって参加した。
rows.en: I joined the resident servants.

ghs.en: when I was mingling with the servitude.
ghs.assessment: Taichi joins the household servants in the cleaning. 'Mingling with the servitude' uses an abstract condition of bondage instead of the people.

highlights.text: when I was mingling with the servitude.

rows.jp: 通いの人間は使わない方針だったためか、人手の貸し借りは茶飯事だった。
rows.en: Perhaps because they had a policy of employing no one who lived off-site, lending one another a hand was routine.

ghs.en:
Perhaps because there was a policy to avoid
using people who don't live in the house, lending
and borrowing of manpower was a common thing.

rows.jp: 十時と三時にお茶の休憩を一時間ずつ挟みながら、順番に部屋を掃除していく。
rows.en: With hour-long tea breaks at ten and three, we cleaned the rooms in order.

ghs.en:
I cleaned the rooms one after the other. It was
an unhurried, well-paced job that also had
one-hour tea breaks at ten and at three.

rows.jp: 夕方には彼女の部屋に辿り着いた。
rows.en: By evening, we had reached her room.

ghs.en: At evening's dusk I had finally reached her room.

rows.jp: はじめて彼女の声を聞いた。
rows.en: I heard her voice for the first time.

ghs.en: I heard her voice for the very first time.

rows.jp: 『……ここはいいわ』
rows.en: “...You can skip this room.”

ghs.en: Youko: 『...no need here.』

rows.jp: 短くそっけない。
rows.en: Brief and curt.

ghs.en: Short and brusque.

rows.jp: 機能的。
rows.en: Functional.

ghs.en: Efficient.

rows.jp: けど、蠱惑的だった。
rows.en: And yet, captivating.

ghs.en: Yet, it was as captivating as magic.
ghs.assessment: 蠱惑的 calls the voice bewitching or seductively captivating. 'Captivating as magic' turns the quality into a simile and loses its alluring register.

highlights.text: Yet, it was as captivating as magic.

rows.jp: ちらりと見た室内は、とても乙女の部屋とは思えない。
rows.en: The glimpse I caught inside looked nothing like a young lady's room.

ghs.en:
A fleeting glance inside her room showed me
something that did not make me think of a
maiden's room at all.

rows.jp: 数台のパソコン。
rows.en: Several computers.

ghs.en: A number of computers,

rows.jp: 四方の壁を覆い隠す本棚と、そこに収まりきらず床に堆(うずたか)く積まれた書物。
rows.en: Bookshelves hiding all four walls, and books stacked high on the floor when the shelves could hold no more.

ghs.en:
walls in all four directions entirely covered
in bookshelves, and as those were insufficient,
tall piles of books on the floor,

rows.jp: 重々しい工作台と、使い込まれた工具。
rows.en: A heavy workbench and well-worn tools.

ghs.en:
a worktable of ponderous look, with tools that
looked very well used.

rows.jp: かなり広い私室は雑多な知識と技術で埋め尽くされていて、秘密基地を連想させた。
rows.en: Her large private room was crammed with a jumble of knowledge and technology. It brought a secret base to mind.

ghs.en:
Her fairly big personal room was completely
buried under miscellaneous knowledge and craft,
and it was reminiscent of a secret base.

rows.jp: なるほど確かに一人だけ異質な者が、異世界にはいたのだ。
rows.en: So in that otherworld, there really was one person who did not belong.

ghs.en:
I see, it's certain, a heterogeneous person
that's always alone dwells in a parallel world.
ghs.assessment: Taichi realizes that one anomalous person existed alone within that otherworld. The English adds that she is 'always alone,' shifts to present tense, and says she dwells in a parallel world.

highlights.text:
I see, it's certain, a heterogeneous person
that's always alone dwells in a parallel world.

rows.jp: 綺麗な衣装を着て、女の子の言葉遣いでお茶の相手をしている時、支倉曜子について問いかけたことがある。
rows.en: Once, dressed in pretty clothes, speaking like a girl, and serving as a tea companion, I asked about Yoko Hasekura.

ghs.en:
In the time when I was wearing a gaudy dress, and
was a tea party companion speaking with a girl's
mannerisms, I did ask about Hasekura Youko.
ghs.assessment: Taichi wears beautiful clothes while speaking in girlish language. 'Gaudy dress' adds a negative judgment not present in 綺麗.

highlights.text:
In the time when I was wearing a gaudy dress, and
was a tea party companion speaking with a girl's
mannerisms, I did ask about Hasekura Youko.

rows.jp: もの静かな老婦人は答えた。
rows.en: A quiet old lady answered.

ghs.en: A very quiet older lady replied,

rows.jp: 末の息子のそのまた娘と。
rows.en: She was the daughter of the youngest son.

ghs.en:
that she is the daughter of the son of the son of
the Head.
ghs.assessment: Youko is the daughter of the youngest son. The English adds another generation, making her the daughter of the son of the Head's son.

highlights.text:
that she is the daughter of the son of the son of
the Head.

rows.jp: 若く快活な婦人は答えた。
rows.en: A young, lively lady answered.

ghs.en: A younger and cheerful adult lady replied,

rows.jp: 望まれて生まれた娘ではないと。
rows.en: She had not been a wanted child.

ghs.en: that she was a daughter born unwanted.

rows.jp: 姦しい三姉妹は囀(さえず)った。
rows.en: Three noisy sisters twittered.

ghs.en: Three boisterous sisters chirped,

rows.jp: 若旦那とうら若き使用人との秘められた恋物語と、その顛末。
rows.en: The secret romance between the young master and a young female servant, and how it ended.

ghs.en:
that it was a secret love story between the young
master and a young servant, and those are the
facts.
ghs.assessment: 顛末 is the course and outcome of the secret relationship. 'Those are the facts' neither describes the outcome nor completes the preceding story phrase.

highlights.text:
that it was a secret love story between the young
master and a young servant, and those are the
facts.

rows.jp: 誰にもなつかず愛を知らない娘の咎と、訪れるであろう悲劇的結末。
rows.en: The sin of a girl who warmed to no one and knew no love, and the tragic ending that must surely await her.

ghs.en:
It was an infamy of a daughter, emotionally
unattached to all, never knowing love, and the
tragic fate likely to come.

rows.jp: 支倉の血でありながら支倉の一員ではない、そんな汚点に対する嘆き。
rows.en: Their laments over the stain of someone who bore Hasekura blood without belonging to the Hasekura family.

ghs.en:
What sadness for the stain of having the blood
of the Hasekura while being not of the Hasekuras.

rows.jp: 要するに忌み子だったのだ。
rows.en: In short, she was a child they considered cursed.

ghs.en: In other words, she was a shunned, taboo child.

rows.jp: 誰も彼女に語りかける者はなく、彼女もまた誰にも語らなかった。
rows.en: No one spoke to her, and she in turn spoke to no one.

ghs.en:
There was no one who would come and address her,
and she, on her own, addressed nobody.

rows.jp: 腫れ物だった。
rows.en: She was a sore spot no one dared touch.

ghs.en: She was a tumor.
ghs.assessment: 腫れ物 figuratively means a sore spot or untouchable person whom everyone handles warily. 'She was a tumor' literalizes the image into a medical growth.

highlights.text: She was a tumor.

rows.jp: 彼女の実父である若旦那なる人物は、海外に留学してしまったそうだ。
rows.en: The young master who was her biological father had apparently gone abroad to study.

ghs.en:
The young master, her real father, seemed to be
studying abroad.
ghs.assessment: The narrator reports that her father had gone abroad to study. 'Seemed to be studying abroad' makes the study contemporaneous rather than the departure a past fact.

highlights.text:
The young master, her real father, seemed to be
studying abroad.

rows.jp: 母親の使用人は……亡くなっていた。
rows.en: Her mother’s servant... was dead.

ghs.en: The servant, her mother... had passed away.

rows.jp: 何者にもなれない少女。
rows.en: A girl who could never become anyone.

ghs.en: A girl that could become no one,

rows.jp: 誰にも求められない少女。
rows.en: A girl no one wanted.

ghs.en: a girl desired by no one.

rows.jp: 傷つく。
rows.en: She would be hurt.

ghs.en: Wounded.

rows.jp: 否。傷つかない。
rows.en: No. She would not be hurt.

ghs.en: Untrue. Not wounded.

rows.jp: 支倉曜子は強かった。
rows.en: Yoko Hasekura was strong.

ghs.en: Hasekura Youko was strong.

rows.jp: 意に介さなかった。
rows.en: She paid it no mind.

ghs.en: She paid no heed.

rows.jp: たぶん気づいていたんだと思う。
rows.en: I think she probably understood.

ghs.en: I think, perhaps, that she had noticed,

rows.jp: 世界が箱庭であることを。
rows.en: That the world was a miniature garden.

ghs.en: how this world was a miniature garden.

rows.jp: 人形生活の合間、俺は図書室に通った。
rows.en: Between spells of doll duty, I went to the library.

ghs.en:
In the spare moments of my life as a doll,
I made my way towards the library.

rows.jp: 影響を受けたのかも知れない。
rows.en: Perhaps she had influenced me.

ghs.en: Maybe she had influenced me, who knows.

rows.jp: 貴婦人からは作法とお茶を学んだ。
rows.en: The ladies taught me manners and tea.

ghs.en:
I studied etiquette and tea ceremony in depth
with the ladies,

rows.jp: けれど知恵と技術と真実は、そこにはなかった。
rows.en: But there was no wisdom, no technology, no truth there.

ghs.en: but in those, wisdom, art and truth there weren't.
ghs.assessment: The ladies offered neither wisdom, technical skill, nor truth. 'Art' is too broad for 技術 here, and 'there weren't' is inverted ungrammatically.

highlights.text: but in those, wisdom, art and truth there weren't.

rows.jp: 補うために、使う者の少ない図書室に通い詰めた。
rows.en: To make up for it, I haunted the seldom-used library.

ghs.en:
To supplement, I frequently visited the rarely
populated library.

rows.jp: 曜子ちゃんとはよく出会った。
rows.en: I often ran into Yoko.

ghs.en: I met Youko-chan frequently,

rows.jp: 依然として会話はない。
rows.en: Still, we never spoke.

ghs.en: yet still without conversation.

rows.jp: なんとなく癪(しゃく)だったので、俺からアプローチすることもなかった。
rows.en: Somehow, that rankled, so I made no approach myself.

ghs.en:
For some annoyance or another, there was no
approach from me either.

rows.jp: 好ましくは思っていたけど、仲良くなりたいと願いはしなかった。
rows.en: I thought well of her, but I did not wish to become friends.

ghs.en:
I thought her as desirable, but I had no wish for
us to become good friends.
ghs.assessment: Taichi thought well of Youko or found her likable. 'Desirable' introduces a stronger sexualized evaluation.

highlights.text:
I thought her as desirable, but I had no wish for
us to become good friends.

rows.jp: 俺の美的傾向は、この頃から確立されたようだ。
rows.en: It seems my aesthetic inclinations were already established by then.

ghs.en:
Seems that my aesthetic sensitivity was formed
right around that time.

rows.jp: なんというか……自立しているものに惹かれた。
rows.en: How can I put it...? I was drawn to things that stood on their own.

ghs.en:
How to say this... I was attracted, charmed, by
what can stand on its own.

rows.jp: 独力で生きるものと、力に。
rows.en: To things that lived by their own power—and to power itself.

ghs.en:
By that strength, the strength that allows living
on one's own.
ghs.assessment: He is drawn to beings that live by their own power and to that power itself. 'By that strength' makes the strength an agent or means acting on him.

highlights.text:
By that strength, the strength that allows living
on one's own.

rows.jp: 知識にしろ技術にしろ、そういう側面がある。
rows.en: Knowledge and technology share that quality.

ghs.en:
Whether it's in the knowledge or whether it's in
the craft, that side of things exists.

rows.jp: 人は群れる。
rows.en: People gather in herds.

ghs.en: Humans flock together.

rows.jp: 群れることを渇望する。
rows.en: They ache to herd together.

ghs.en: They crave flocking itself.

rows.jp: そして同時に、聖域を持とうとする。
rows.en: At the same time, they try to preserve a sanctuary.

ghs.en:
And then, simultaneously, they want to have a holy
ground, a sanctuary.

rows.jp: 侵害されない自分のための場所を欲する。
rows.en: They want a place of their own that cannot be violated.

ghs.en:
They desire a place for themselves that
is never infringed.

rows.jp: しかし人と接すれば境界線は揺らぐ。
rows.en: But contact with others makes the border waver.

ghs.en:
Yet when people come into contact, the boundary
lines waver.

rows.jp: 領土は減ったり増えたりする。
rows.en: Territory shrinks and expands.

ghs.en:
The size of this domain maybe decreases, maybe
increases.
ghs.assessment: Personal territory shrinks and expands as boundaries shift. 'Maybe decreases, maybe increases' changes the general dynamic into uncertainty.

highlights.text:
The size of this domain maybe decreases, maybe
increases.

rows.jp: 不快。
rows.en: Unpleasant.

rows.en: He made straight men use me while I was dressed as a little girl.

ghs.en:
I, who looked like a little girl, was made into
his straight male partner.
ghs.assessment: S makes straight men engage with the cross-dressed Taichi. 'His straight male partner' makes Taichi the partner of S and collapses the other men into a possessive modifier.

highlights.text:
I, who looked like a little girl, was made into
his straight male partner.

rows.jp: 冗談半分でやる者が大半だった。
rows.en: Most of them did it half as a joke.

ghs.en:
People who liked to half-jest were more than
the half there.
ghs.assessment: Most participants did it half as a joke. The English instead describes people who liked to half-jest and then compares their number to a half.

highlights.text:
People who liked to half-jest were more than
the half there.

rows.jp: たまに覚醒してしまう者もいたが。
rows.en: Though every so often, one of them awakened to something.

ghs.en:
Occasionally, there were people who grew
disillusioned, but,
ghs.assessment: 覚醒 means that some participants awakened to or discovered a new appetite. 'Grew disillusioned' means they lost belief or enthusiasm, the opposite direction.

highlights.text:
Occasionally, there were people who grew
disillusioned, but,

rows.jp: 夜会では、どんなえげつないことをするかが、目立つのポイントだった。
rows.en: At the parties, you stood out by doing something especially depraved.

ghs.en:
at the evening parties the point was always to
stand out via whatever dirty or disgraceful act.

rows.jp: 小学校のいじめとかでも、似たようなことが起こる。
rows.en: Something similar happens with bullying in elementary school.

ghs.en:
What happened there was something similar
to elementary school bullying.
ghs.assessment: The narrator generalizes that similar behavior occurs in elementary-school bullying. The English changes this to a comparison with a specific past event.

highlights.text:
What happened there was something similar
to elementary school bullying.

rows.jp: 集団の中では、かなりの高確率でこういうことは発生する。
rows.en: Within a group, this kind of thing happens with fairly high probability.

ghs.en:
Inside of a group, there is a fairly high chance
that this sort of things would happen.
ghs.assessment: 'This sort of things' mismatches singular 'sort' and plural 'things.'

highlights.text:
Inside of a group, there is a fairly high chance
that this sort of things would happen.

rows.jp: ま、デメリットというやつだ。
rows.en: Well, that is what you call a downside.

ghs.en: Well, let's call that a demerit then.

rows.jp: 物事にはメリットデメリットが必ずある。
rows.en: Everything comes with advantages and disadvantages.

ghs.en:
Everything without exception has merits and
demerits, pros and cons,

rows.jp: 一義的な善し悪しを越えてだ。
rows.en: Beyond any simple question of good or bad.

ghs.en: beyond the unambiguous good and bad.

rows.jp: やがてＳのＳっぷりはエスカレート。
rows.en: Before long, S's S-ness escalated.

ghs.en: Before long, the S-style of our S escalated.

rows.jp: 子供を連れてきた。
rows.en: He brought a child.

ghs.en: He brought in a child,

rows.jp: Ｓの息子だ。
rows.en: S's son.

ghs.en: the son of S.

rows.jp: 学校ではいじめっ子としてならしていた……らしい。
rows.en: At school, he had apparently made a name for himself as a bully.

ghs.en: It seemed at school he was a bully... of sorts.
ghs.assessment: The boy was reputed or notorious as a bully at school. 'A bully of sorts' weakens the established reputation into uncertainty about whether he qualified.

highlights.text: It seemed at school he was a bully... of sorts.

rows.jp: 乱交の雰囲気に圧倒されていたのも束の間、俺を見て嘲笑った。
rows.en: The atmosphere of the orgy overwhelmed him, but only for a moment. Then he saw me and sneered.

ghs.en:
In the brief moment of being overwhelmed by
the promiscuity in the air, he looked at me
and sneered in ridicule.
ghs.assessment: After only a brief spell of being overwhelmed, the boy sees Taichi and sneers. 'In the brief moment ... he looked' makes the reaction simultaneous rather than subsequent.

highlights.text:
In the brief moment of being overwhelmed by
the promiscuity in the air, he looked at me
and sneered in ridicule.

rows.jp: 異常興奮からか。
rows.en: Perhaps the frenzy had gotten to him.

ghs.en: Because he was abnormally excited, maybe.

rows.jp: 促されるまま、むしろ積極的に、そいつは参加した。
rows.en: Prompted by the others, he joined in—eagerly, even.

ghs.en:
This guy participated, under peer pressure
but fairly proactively.

rows.jp: 血を引いているようで、すぐ才能を発揮しはじめた。
rows.en: It seemed to run in the blood. His talent soon began to show.

ghs.en:
As if inherited in the blood, he soon began
to display his talent.

rows.jp: 早熟な精通と重なっていたせいもあるだろうか。
rows.en: Perhaps it was also because this coincided with his precocious first ejaculation.

ghs.en:
Perhaps it's also the accumulation of all
this precocious knowledge to blame.
ghs.assessment: 早熟な精通 refers to precocious sexual maturation or first ejaculation. 'Accumulation of all this precocious knowledge' misreads 精通 as expertise and invents accumulation.

highlights.text:
Perhaps it's also the accumulation of all
this precocious knowledge to blame.

rows.jp: じき夢中になった。
rows.en: Before long, he was absorbed in it.

ghs.en: He quickly got hooked.

rows.jp: 俺は皆に笑われた。
rows.en: Everyone laughed at me.

ghs.en: I was ridiculed by all.

rows.jp: 笑われながら、何週間も。
rows.en: For weeks, while they laughed,

ghs.en:
I kept being ridiculed,
and for so many weeks,

rows.jp: 俺は攻撃を受け続けた。
rows.en: I endured one assault after another.

ghs.en:
I continued to take
their attacks.
